label: spec-forge describing itself
what: The answers that describe this project, so the tool can write its own three files through the template path with no model. If this file stops regenerating a complete spec, the tool has stopped being able to describe itself.

answers.text: spec-forge is a local-first interview that turns a portfolio project into three files a person can hand to someone else: proposal.md, design.md and tasks.md. It asks about nine topics, fires follow-up questions when an answer mentions something specific, and assembles the files from the answers alone. No backend, no API key, no account.

Project specs die in two ways. A person writes them in a document nobody reopens, or an assistant writes them and quietly invents details that sound authoritative. Both end with a file that is not true, which is worse than no file: the reader cannot tell which sentences were checked.

People write a README at the end, or paste a prompt into a chat window and copy out whatever comes back. The README is honest and incomplete, the chat transcript is complete and unverifiable, and neither survives the next round of edits.

Produce three files a reviewer can act on, where every sentence can be traced to the answer it came from, and where the tool refuses to hand over a document that contains an unreviewed guess. One developer fills it in one sitting and downloads all three files.

A person who has never seen the project reads proposal.md and can state what it does and who it is for, without asking a follow-up. The export gate blocks with a named reason every time the document holds an inferred block nobody reviewed.

- Initial bundle: under 500 kB raw, measured on every build
- Suite: 610 specs, and the gate under 2 s with one staged file
- Model: 4096 tokens of context and 879 MB for the default weights
- Network: zero requests after the first load

- Angular 20 with standalone components and signals
- TypeScript strict with strictTemplates
- CodeMirror 6 for the block editors
- idb for the draft store
- fflate for the zip, behind a dynamic import
- Karma and Jasmine for the suite
- Docker and nginx for the static serve

- Not a collaborative editor
- Not a project tracker
- Not a resume builder
- Does not publish, deploy or read a repository
- No account and nothing to sign in to

The real risk is trusting a generated sentence because it reads well. The mitigation is structural rather than editorial: provenance on every block, a gate that blocks on unreviewed inferences, snapshots before every regeneration and a diff a person has to accept section by section.
4096 tokens per file, and the budget check refuses a run that would not fit rather than truncating the prompt in silence.
The default model costs 879 MB and the recommended one 3.4 GB, both shown next to the name before anything is downloaded.
Without WebGPU the model runs on WASM at 5 to 20 times slower, and the app says so in a banner instead of appearing to hang.
